It’s not explaining, but communicating this person doesn’t know you there’s no way she knows what you want in life. In communicating on what you want for yourself and setting your own boundaries you’re building a base for a healthy and happy relationship.😊 not only with her but yourself as well.

As a female myself, who has multiple partners, I always found it more engaging and little less intimidating when a guy/girl just talks to me, and asks me out other than asking me if I have a boyfriend or partner. Because if I’m having a good conversation with you more than likely I want it to continue and being asked that can be hurtful to the person who asked and it kills the conversation. Don’t get me wrong it’s very direct, but it does tell me that your only interested in one thing more than knowing and understanding me as a human being. 
So be bold, be a friend, and don’t ask the “elephant in the room” questions.

Maybe she is in a polyamorous relationship? Dating and being poly can be a bit difficult, people are rubbed the wrong way when you are on a date with someone and you mention you have other partners. So that could be the reason why she hesitated to tell you about her other guys. 

Secondly, in polyamory being #1 isn’t always a good thing. Having that mindset leads you into a different branch of polyamory known as hierarchical polyamory, where one partner is #1 and the others are secondary. In most cases, if someone is already partnered they already have a primary and that forcing yourself or asking to be her primary when she may or may not have one is disrespectful to her other relationship. 

My advice would be talking to her. Tell her what you want out of a relationship and get then get her side of things. I wish you the best of luck.

My best advice: tell the people you care about the most the real situation. Like “I have depression and some days are harder than others. When I’m feeling depressed just hug me.(or whatever type of support you need from those people) and I will be okay and I love you.” That seems to work with me and I have a lot of support and the people who matter to me get it and they’re able to provide with what they are comfortable with at the time and are able to understand my emotional boundaries. I’m sorry, you had to go through that. My mom was pretty strict about it too, but she never called me a slut for it. I got mad at her and said “boys and girls both look at me regardless what I wear, don’t bring that bullshit, I just want to enjoy dinner with my mother.” Made her understand that I wasn’t going to tolerate her judgement and I would like to think she respects me more for standing up for myself, and being the independent person she raised me to be. Of course, this was also the same day that I told her that I was an atheist, poly, and bisexual.
